title: Lightning in the night
hookLine: a kind idea flares up in the shower and is gone by breakfast; Shantideva knew why
carry: goodness flashes like lightning; the awakening mind holds it
tomorrow: what could turn an ordinary body into gold?

lines: A GOOD THOUGHT IN THE SHOWER.
cards: Somewhere in the shower, a good thought arrives: call your aunt, she's been lonely. Or: that new kid eats lunch alone, sit with him. It's clear and warm and completely obvious.
Then you dry off, the phone buzzes, and by breakfast it's gone so cleanly you can't remember having it. Why does that happen? Shantideva has an answer, and it's an odd one.
He doesn't pick a candle or a sunrise for a good thought. He picks lightning.

teach.h: A DARK NIGHT, THICK WITH CLOUDS.
teach.b: Here's the verse, in plain words.

On a dark night thick with clouds, lightning shows everything for a moment. In the same way, now and then, through the Buddha's power, the world's mind turns toward good for a moment. So that's the puzzle: why lightning?
A good thought could have been a lamp, something steady you carry around. Shantideva chose the opposite on purpose. Lightning has two properties.
It's brief, gone before you can point. And while it lasts, you see the whole landscape: the road, the fence, the ditch you were about to step in. That's what a good thought does.
For one second you see clearly what to do, then the night closes back in. Notice who gets the credit, too. The verse doesn't say you're a good person for having it.
It says the flash comes, now and then, by the Buddha's power, like weather. The next verse is blunt: so goodness is weak and the pull the other way is strong.

Then Shantideva asks what could hold the light. His answer, the mind set on awakening for everyone, is where the rest of this chapter goes. For today, the move is smaller: when the flash comes, look while it lasts.

how: Students of the Bodhicaryavatara often memorize this verse, and some Mahayana teachers use it to encourage acting on a kind impulse right away, before it fades.

games.q: what does “lightning in the night” mean?
o: a frightening warning sent at the worst possible moment
a good thought: rare, quick, and it shows the whole road
a sudden burst of anger that passes in a flash

games.q: the lightning verse — tap the pairs.
p: the mind most of the time
a good thought, here for a moment
where the verse says the flash comes from
goodness is weak, the other pull is strong

s: a good thought that fades means you weren't sincere
the verse expects the flash to be brief. it's the nature of lightning, not a mark against you.
the verse says the flash comes now and then, through the Buddha's power
Shantideva doesn't make it your achievement; it arrives, like weather.
Shantideva compares a good thought to a steady lamp
he picks lightning on purpose: brief, but you see everything while it lasts.

games.q: in the middle of a work meeting you get a flash: your coworker looked upset this morning, check on her. what fits the verse?
o: make a note and send her a quick message right after the meeting.
wait until you feel the urge more strongly, so it's real.
ignore it; good thoughts come back if they're important.
games.why: lightning doesn't come back on schedule. the verse says look while it lasts: the flash shows you the road, so take a step while you can still see it.

practice: Close your eyes and let thoughts come and go for a while. You're waiting for one kind thought, about anyone, however small.
When it flashes, don't chase the next thing: stay with that one, look at it clearly, and see what it's asking you to do.

wordCard.voice: Lightning in the night: Shantideva's picture of a good thought. Rare, quick, and while it lasts, you can see the whole road.

orig.note: Sanskrit: lightning. Shantideva's verse uses it for a good thought that lights everything for a moment.

carryVoice: Carry this: goodness flashes like lightning; the awakening mind holds it. Brief, but bright enough to see the road by. That's day three of the poem.

sources.ref: Bodhicaryavatara 1.5 (lightning on a dark, cloudy night)
Bodhicaryavatara 1.6 (goodness is weak; what but the awakening mind could overcome the other pull)
